title: Prior Goodwill and Corrective Entries and the Rounding of a Personal Checking Take-Back
content:
Two cases take the take-back on a Personal Checking account to a finer figure, both read from the entries granted to the account in the last twelve months, from the owner's certificate principal held under Certificates of Deposit, and from the owner's card payments under Personal Credit Cards.

- Where a goodwill or corrective entry has been granted to the account in the last twelve months **and** the owner holds any certificate principal, the take-back is taken to the cent.
- Where the case above does not apply **and** either at least 3 such entries have been granted in the last twelve months **or** the owner has made at least 15 card payments in the last twelve months, the take-back is taken in whole dollars, rounded half-up.
- Where neither case applies, the take-back is not taken to either of those finer figures.

**Worked rounding on hypothetical inputs.** Take a figure of 172.63 before rounding.

| Owner's position | Take-back |
|---|---|
| 1 goodwill entry in the last twelve months, certificate principal of 4000.00 | 172.63 |
| 1 goodwill entry in the last twelve months, no certificate principal | 173.00 only where a further limb of the second case is met |
| 4 goodwill or corrective entries in the last twelve months, no certificate principal | 173.00 |
| No such entries, 17 card payments in the last twelve months | 173.00 |
| No such entries, 5 card payments | Neither case applies |

The first case counts a single such entry and needs certificate principal above zero alongside it; the second counts at least 3 of them, or reaches its card payment limb instead. Equality satisfies each threshold.
